column3: “City of bloods” is rendered “bloody city”; NASB supplies “completely.”
NASB renders the noun phrases as clauses (“Swords flashing, spears gleaming”), and “no end to the bodies” as “countless dead bodies.”
“Good of grace” is rendered “The charming one,” and “clans” “families”; NASB adds “All.”
“Detestable things” is rendered “filth,” and “treat with contempt” “make you vile.”
“The canals” is rendered “the waters of the Nile”; “made good more than” is rendered “better than,” and “from sea” “consisted of the sea.”
“Cush” is rendered “Ethiopia,” and “the Libyans” “Lubim”; “your help” is rendered “her helpers.”
“Children” is rendered “small children,” and “honored people” “honorable men.”
“Certainly opened” is rendered “opened wide,” and “bars” “gate bars.”
The Hebrew uses two locust words; NASB renders them “creeping locust” and “swarming locust.”
“Courtiers” is rendered “guardsmen,” “officials” “marshals,” and “a locust of locusts” “hordes of grasshoppers”; NASB supplies “stone” before “walls.”
“Fracture” is rendered “breakdown,” and “severe” “incurable”; “strike a palm” is rendered “clap their hands.”
